claim.why_it_matters: Every sub-entry indent on this page is dropped. The five opening lines are indented in the PDF because they continue the 'Transfer of control 539' entry begun at the foot of page 1257; flattened, 'GOBACK statement 540, 631' reads as a top-level index entry with no connection to transfer of control. verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, and the claim misquotes neither source.

PDF (rendered at 300 dpi, then cropped and magnified 1.5x-2x to measure the left edges directly): the five opening lines GOBACK statement 540, 631 / MERGE statement 539 / PERFORM statement 540 / SORT statement 539 / STOP statement 540 all begin at a left edge visibly inset from the column margin, while the very next line 'TRIM function 932' and the following 'TRUE phrase' begin flush at the margin. The same one-level inset is printed for 'EVALUATE directive 66' / 'EVALUATE statement 618' / 'SET statement, condition setting 730' under 'TRUE phrase'; for 'DEFAULT ROUNDED clause 273' / 'INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause 278' / 'ROUNDED phrase 560' under 'TRUNCATION phrase'; for 'Data description entry 363' under 'TYPEDEF clause 500'; for 'Scope of 148' and 'TYPE clause 494' under the flush-left 'Type-name 98, 103'; for 'Definition of 165' under 'Types'; and throughout the right column (e.g. 'SET statement 731' under 'USER-DEFAULT phrase'; 'Definition 97' and 'Notation 980' under 'User-defined words'; the two separate 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 291' lines under 'UTF-16 19, 153' and 'UTF-8 108'). The indentation is a real printed two-level index hierarchy, not an artifact of the render.

Markdown (raw bytes of specs/ISO_COBOL.md between the page-1258 and page-1259 anchors, inspected with repr so whitespace cannot hide): all 113 non-blank lines start at column 0. Zero lines carry leading space or tab. The same scan over pages 1249-1259 returns 0 indented lines out of ~1189 non-blank lines, so the claim's 'same systematic defect as pages 1249-1257' is also accurate.

The page-1257 premise checks out too: that page's markdown tail is 'Transfer of control [539]' followed by 'EXIT FUNCTION statement 540 / EXIT PROGRAM statement 540 / EXIT statement 539', and page 1258 resumes that same alphabetical sub-list at GOBACK. So the five opening lines are indeed continuation sub-entries of 'Transfer of control'.

This is not page-break furniture, reflow, wrapping, or hyphenation. No text is missing and nothing is reordered - but in an index, indentation is the ONLY encoding of the parent/child relation, so flattening it is a loss of data, not of decoration, and it manufactures statements the standard does not make: (a) 'GOBACK statement 540, 631' becomes a bogus top-level entry sitting between S- and T- headwords, alphabetically impossible and severed from 'Transfer of control'; (b) 'TYPE clause 494' on line 26 becomes a second top-level 'TYPE clause' entry contradicting line 21's 'TYPE clause 478, 494'; (c) 'Definition of 165' detaches from 'Types', 'SET statement 731' from 'USER-DEFAULT phrase', and two identical 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 291' lines detach from UTF-16 and UTF-8 respectively. Real discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but the 'kind' label is wrong and the practical impact should be scoped. Nothing is MISPLACED - no text is missing, moved, or reordered, and the two-column linearization (left column through 'UPPER-CASE function 934', then right column from 'Uppercase letters 90') is correct. The actual defect is LOST STRUCTURE / FLATTENED HIERARCHY: the transcription discards the one-level sub-entry indentation that the PDF prints, on all 113 non-blank lines of page 1258 and on all of pages 1249-1259 (0 indented lines out of ~1189). Everything the claim asserts about the mechanism is verified, including that the five opening lines continue the 'Transfer of control 539' entry begun at the foot of page 1257. Beyond the cited examples, the flattening also detaches 'Definition of 165' from 'Types', 'SET statement 731' from 'USER-DEFAULT phrase', 'Definition 97'/'Notation 980' from 'User-defined words', and the two 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 291' lines from 'UTF-16' and 'UTF-8'; and it creates a false duplicate, since flattened 'TYPE clause 494' (line 26) now contradicts the genuine top-level 'TYPE clause 478, 494' (line 21). Scope caveat for triage: this is the alphabetical back-matter index, not normative language text - no syntax diagram, general rule, or semantic definition is affected, so the damage is to index navigability and to any tooling that consumes the index as a structured entry/sub-entry map, not to derived COBOL behavior. 'structural' is a fair severity on that basis; it should not be read as a normative-text defect.
